report.title: OpenAI ships GPT-5.6 and GPT-5.6 Pro today
report.summary: GPT-5.6 and GPT-5.6 Pro were rumored for today's launch, with leaked codename 'kindle-alpha' clearing staging and stealth tests already running inside ChatGPT Pro accounts. Reported spec bumps: 1.5M token context window, stronger agentic coding, Playwright-native browser testing, and a redesigned reward-audit pipeline meant to prevent the cross-persona alignment failure that contaminated GPT-5.5 training data. Pricing is said to be roughly 5x cheaper than Anthropic's Fable 5. No official OpenAI release note confirmed at time of publication — verify at openai.com/news before integrating.

report.title: OpenAI retires GPT-4.5 from ChatGPT on June 27
report.summary: GPT-4.5 exits ChatGPT for paid users on June 27, 2026, following a 30-day sunset. The API is unaffected, but any ChatGPT-based workflow defaulting to GPT-4.5 will auto-migrate — check your model settings before the weekend.

report.title: OpenAI ships GPT-5.5-Cyber with record CyberGym score
report.summary: GPT-5.5-Cyber launched June 22 as part of OpenAI's Daybreak cybersecurity initiative, hitting 85.6% on CyberGym and 39.5% on ExploitGym — both record scores. Access is gated to vetted partners including Akamai, Cloudflare, CrowdStrike, and Palo Alto Networks; no public API endpoint.

report.title: Gemini 3.5 Pro still stuck in enterprise preview as GA window closes
report.summary: Google's Gemini 3.5 Pro remains limited Vertex AI preview as of June 25, the final day of Sundar Pichai's 'give us until next month' promise from Google I/O. Confirmed specs when it does land: 2M token context window, Deep Think reasoning mode behind the $250/month Ultra tier, estimated $15/$60 per million token pricing. No public model ID published yet.

report.title: Fable 5 export ban redirects non-US builders to GLM-5.2
report.summary: A June 12 US government directive suspended international access to Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5, pushing non-US teams toward GLM-5.2 from Z.ai — MIT-licensed, 1M context, SWE-bench Pro score of 62.1 beating GPT-5.5's 58.6, at $1.40/$4.40 per million tokens. Self-hosting requires at minimum eight H100 GPUs.

report.title: MiniMax M3 ships as first open-weight model with frontier coding, 1M context, and multimodal
report.summary: MiniMax M3 launched June 1 with 59% SWE-bench Pro (edging GPT-5.5's 58.6%), a 1M-token context window via novel MSA sparse attention, and native image/video input — the first open-weight model to combine all three. API pricing started at $0.30/$1.20 per million tokens on OpenRouter promo; weights hit Hugging Face roughly ten days post-launch under a commercial-use license that requires review before production deployment.

report.title: Claude Tag brings @Claude into Slack with task assignment
report.summary: Anthropic shipped Claude Tag, letting teams add Claude to any Slack channel by tagging @Claude and assigning it work directly in-thread. Internally it already generates 65% of code on Anthropic's own product team — a useful signal for teams evaluating async agent workflows over chat.

learn.name: Headroom
learn.oneLineDescription: Compress tool outputs, logs, and RAG chunks 60-95% before they hit the LLM.

detail.whatItDoes:
Headroom is an open-source context compression layer that preprocesses tool outputs, system logs, raw files, and RAG-retrieved chunks before they are sent to an LLM. It strips redundancy and non-essential content while preserving semantic integrity, achieving 60-95% token reduction with claimed identical answer quality.

It ships in three integration modes: a Python library for inline use inside your own code, an HTTP proxy that transparently compresses any LLM request pipeline, and an MCP server so any MCP-compatible agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) can compress context without code changes.
detail.whoItsFor: Engineers running agentic coding pipelines (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) where tool call outputs and file reads are burning context budget. Particularly valuable for RAG pipelines returning large document chunks, CI/CD agents looping over verbose logs, and teams hitting rate limits or token cost ceilings on paid API tiers.
pros: 60-95% token reduction directly lowers API costs and extends effective context window
Three deployment modes (library, proxy, MCP server) fit most stack architectures without refactoring
Zero-dependency on any specific LLM provider — works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and local models
10K+ GitHub stars in weeks, active issue tracker, real-world validation from Claude Code and Cursor users
cons: Compression quality on highly structured or code-heavy outputs is unverified at scale; benchmark claims are self-reported
Proxy mode adds a network hop and a potential single point of failure in production pipelines
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Python 3.10+
- An existing LLM API key (Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.)

## Option 1: Library (inline, fastest to try)

```bash
pip install headroom
```

```python
from headroom import compress

# Compress a tool output string before inserting into a prompt
raw_log = open("build.log").read()  # e.g. 50K tokens of CI output
compressed = compress(raw_log)

# Drop compressed into your messages array as usual
messages = [
    {"role": "user", "content": f"Debug this build:\n{compressed}"}
]
```

**Gotcha:** `compress()` is lossy by design — always test on your actual data before deploying to production. Structured JSON tool outputs compress well; tightly formatted code diffs may degrade.

## Option 2: MCP Server (zero-code change for Claude Code / Codex)

```bash
# Install
pip install headroom

# Start the MCP server
headroom serve --port 8765
```

Then add to your `claude_code_settings.json` or `~/.codex/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "headroom": {
      "url": "http://localhost:8765"
    }
  }
}
```

Restart your agent. All tool call responses will be compressed transparently before reaching the model.

## Option 3: HTTP Proxy (drop-in for any LLM client)

```bash
# Run proxy on port 4000, forwarding to Anthropic
headroom proxy --upstream https://api.anthropic.com --port 4000
```

```bash
# Point your client at localhost:4000 instead
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4000
```

**Gotcha for proxy mode:** You must pass your real API key through the proxy. Check the Headroom docs for the `--passthrough-auth` flag if your client adds auth headers that conflict.

learn.name: Claude Tag (Slack)
learn.oneLineDescription: Add @Claude to your Slack workspace as a persistent team member that handles async tasks.

detail.whatItDoes:
Claude Tag lets teams add Claude as a named participant in Slack channels. Admins grant Claude access to specific channels and connect it to tools, data sources, and codebases. Anyone in the channel can then @-mention Claude to delegate a task — it picks up context from the channel history, executes using its connected tools, and posts results asynchronously.

Claude builds a persistent memory of channel context over time, learning team preferences, recurring workflows, and project state. It is powered by Opus 4.8 and sits on top of the same agentic infrastructure as Claude Code, meaning it can run subagents, use MCP servers, and plan multi-step tasks.
detail.whoItsFor: Engineering and product teams on Claude Enterprise or Team plans who already use Slack as a coordination layer. Particularly suited for teams doing repeated code reviews, codebase Q&A, incident response triage, or documentation updates — tasks where the workflow is well-defined but the requester is not a developer sitting at a terminal.
pros: Async by default — delegate a task and context-switch; Claude posts results when done
Persistent channel memory means Claude learns your project conventions over time without reprompting
Same underlying model and tool access as Claude Code; not a stripped-down chatbot
Enterprise-grade access controls: admins choose which channels and which tools Claude can see
cons: Beta — currently Enterprise and Team plan only, no individual Pro support at launch
Channel memory is Anthropic-managed cloud storage; teams with strict data residency requirements should review terms before enabling
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Claude Enterprise or Team plan
- Slack workspace admin access
- Claude Code access (included with Team plan Standard seats as of recent update)

## Setup Steps

### 1. Enable Claude Tag in Claude Console

```
1. Go to console.anthropic.com
2. Navigate to Integrations > Claude Tag
3. Click "Connect to Slack"
4. Authorize the OAuth flow for your Slack workspace
```

### 2. Invite Claude to a channel

```
# In Slack, in the target channel:
/invite @Claude
```

### 3. Connect tools (optional but recommended)

```
# Back in Claude Console:
# Integrations > Claude Tag > Configure Tools
# Add MCP servers, GitHub, or other connectors
# Scope them to specific channels as needed
```

### 4. Delegate your first task

```
# In Slack:
@Claude review the last 3 PRs merged to main and summarize any risky changes

@Claude check our open GitHub issues labeled "bug" and triage them by severity
```

**Gotcha:** Claude Tag uses Opus 4.8 by default, which counts against your plan's Opus token quota. Heavy async usage can burn through credits faster than interactive Claude.ai sessions — monitor usage in Console > Analytics for the first week.

**Gotcha 2:** Claude builds memory from channel history it can see *after* being invited. It does not backfill historical messages before the invitation date.

learn.name: Gemini CLI
learn.oneLineDescription: Google's open-source terminal AI agent — 1M context, MCP support, free personal quota.

detail.whatItDoes:
Gemini CLI is an Apache 2.0 TypeScript terminal agent from Google that runs a ReAct (reason-and-act) loop with built-in tools: Google Search grounding, file operations, shell command execution, and web fetching. It supports MCP servers for custom tool integrations and uses a GEMINI.md context file for persistent per-project instructions.

It targets the same workflow as Claude Code and Codex CLI — autonomous coding, codebase Q&A, and multi-step task execution from the terminal. Note: as of June 18, 2026, free consumer access (Google AI Pro/Ultra/free Code Assist) has been migrated to the closed-source Antigravity CLI. The open-source Gemini CLI repo remains active for enterprise/API-key users and the open-source community.
detail.whoItsFor: Developers who want an open-source, inspectable coding agent that runs locally in their terminal with a Gemini API key or Google Cloud Vertex AI credentials. Good for teams that need to self-host or audit the agent code. Enterprise users on Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise plans retain full Gemini CLI access unchanged.
pros: Apache 2.0 — fully inspectable, forkable, and self-hostable; no closed-source binary risk
1M token context window with Gemini 3 models via API key
MCP support and GEMINI.md project context files; ecosystem of 100+ community extensions already published
105K+ GitHub stars with 1,100+ contributors; actively maintained by Google
cons: Free consumer tier (personal Google account) was sunset June 18, 2026 — now requires paid API key or enterprise license for ongoing use
Closed-source Antigravity CLI is Google's new consumer product; Gemini CLI's free-tier replacement has aggressive weekly quota limits per community reports
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Node.js 20+
- A Google AI Studio API key (free at aistudio.google.com) OR a Vertex AI service account key

## Quickstart (no install, one-shot)

```bash
export GOOGLE_API_KEY="YOUR_AI_STUDIO_KEY"
npx @google/gemini-cli
```

## Permanent install

```bash
npm install -g @google/gemini-cli

# Verify
gemini --version
```

## Configure your API key

```bash
# Option A: AI Studio key (simplest for individuals)
export GOOGLE_API_KEY="YOUR_AI_STUDIO_KEY"
gemini

# Option B: Vertex AI (for enterprise/GCP billing)
export GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=true
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT="your-project-id"
gcloud auth application-default login
gemini
```

## Add project context (GEMINI.md)

```bash
# In your repo root:
cat > GEMINI.md << 'EOF'
# Project: MyApp
- Language: TypeScript, Node 20
- Test runner: vitest
- Branching: always create a feature branch before editing
- Do not modify package-lock.json manually
EOF

gemini "add error handling to all API routes"
```

## Add an MCP server

```bash
# Edit ~/.gemini/settings.json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "github": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"],
      "env": { "GITHUB_TOKEN": "your-pat" }
    }
  }
}
```

**Gotcha:** If you are on a free personal Google account after June 18, 2026, your requests now route to Antigravity CLI, not Gemini CLI. To use the open-source Gemini CLI, you **must** supply an explicit `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or Vertex AI credentials. The `gemini` binary from a global npm install will still work correctly if credentials are set.

learn.name: Codex Sites + Role Plugins
learn.oneLineDescription: Codex now builds and hosts internal apps from a prompt; six role plugins for 62 SaaS tools.

detail.whatItDoes:
OpenAI shipped two capabilities together on June 2. Role Plugins bundle 62 popular business apps (Snowflake, Salesforce, HubSpot, Figma, Databricks, Tableau, and more) with 110 pre-built agentic skills into six domain packs: Data Analytics, Sales, Equity Investing, Investment Banking, Design, and Software Engineering. Install a plugin and Codex understands your tool's API surface without custom configuration.

Codex Sites (preview for Business/Enterprise) lets Codex generate and host interactive internal web apps — dashboards, scenario planners, project boards, review hubs — available at a workspace URL. Teams can update the app by prompting Codex rather than touching code.
detail.whoItsFor: Enterprise teams on ChatGPT Business or Enterprise plans who want Codex to operate inside their existing SaaS stack without building custom MCP servers or API integrations. Data analysts, sales ops, and finance teams are the stated primary users; non-developers already make up 20% of Codex's 5M weekly active users.
pros: 62 pre-wired SaaS integrations available at plugin install — no custom glue code for standard tools
Sites removes the need for a front-end developer for lightweight internal dashboards
Annotations let users make surgical edits to documents, spreadsheets, and slides without regenerating the whole artifact
Plugin ecosystem is explicitly opening to third-party partners — a growing catalog expected
cons: Sites is preview-only with no published usage caps or approval workflow; governance must be defined manually by admins before broad rollout
Business/Enterprise plan required — no access for individual ChatGPT Plus users at launch
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- ChatGPT Business or Enterprise plan
- Workspace admin access to enable Sites
- Codex app installed (codex.openai.com or via ChatGPT sidebar)

## Install a Role Plugin

```
1. Open the Codex app
2. Click the plugin icon in the sidebar
3. Browse the plugin directory
4. Select a role plugin (e.g., "Data Analytics")
5. Click Install — Codex will walk you through connecting accounts
```

**Example prompt after installing Data Analytics plugin:**
```
Pull last month's revenue by product line from Snowflake and build a 
week-over-week trend chart. Export as a Hex notebook.
```

## Enable Codex Sites (Enterprise admin)

```
1. Go to ChatGPT Admin Console
2. Settings > Features > Sites
3. Enable Sites and configure RBAC — choose which roles can create Sites
```

## Build a Site from a prompt

```
# In the Codex composer:
"Create a sales pipeline dashboard showing open deals by stage,
ACV by rep, and time-in-stage heatmap. Make it shareable with the
sales team by URL."
```

Codex will generate, deploy, and return a workspace URL. To update:
```
# Iterate by prompting directly:
"Add a filter for deal owner and a 30/60/90 day forecast panel."
```

**Gotcha:** Sites uses workspace identity, not SAML. Any workspace member with the link can view — confirm with your security team before sharing dashboards containing sensitive pipeline data. Published usage caps are not documented; monitor token credits during the preview period.

learn.name: Claude Managed Agents (Dreaming + Multiagent)
learn.oneLineDescription: Cloud-hosted Claude agents with persistent memory, parallel subagents, and webhook callbacks.

detail.whatItDoes:
Claude Managed Agents on the Claude Platform adds four production-ready capabilities for cloud-hosted agents. Dreaming is a scheduled background process that reviews past agent sessions, identifies patterns, and curates a persistent memory store — agents improve between runs without manual prompt engineering. Multiagent orchestration lets a lead agent decompose work and dispatch specialist subagents working in parallel on a shared filesystem, each with its own model, prompt, and tool access, with the full execution trace visible in Claude Console.

Outcomes lets you record what happened after an agent run (success, failure, partial) and feed that signal back to improve future sessions. Webhooks deliver agent lifecycle events to your own infrastructure for integration with CI/CD, alerting, and audit systems.
detail.whoItsFor: Backend engineers and platform teams building production agentic workflows on Anthropic's platform — particularly those running multi-day coding tasks, large codebase migrations, or research pipelines that need to improve from run to run. Also valuable for teams evaluating whether to self-host agent orchestration versus using Anthropic's managed infrastructure.
pros: Dreaming eliminates manual memory management — the platform curates agent memory automatically between runs
Parallel subagents on a shared filesystem match the multi-worker patterns most teams build by hand in LangGraph or CrewAI
Full execution trace in Claude Console without standing up your own observability stack
Doubled Claude Code rate limits shipped alongside this release
cons: Managed execution means Anthropic-controlled sandboxes — teams with strict data residency or air-gap requirements must use the self-hosted sandbox option instead
Dreaming memory curation is automatic and not fully transparent; what gets remembered vs. discarded is not yet user-configurable
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Claude API key (claude.ai API or Anthropic Console)
- `anthropic` Python SDK >= latest (`pip install --upgrade anthropic`)
- A Claude Enterprise, Team, or pay-as-you-go API account

## Install / upgrade SDK

```bash
pip install --upgrade anthropic
```

## Launch a Managed Agent with Dreaming enabled

```python
import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic()

# Create a managed agent session with dreaming enabled
session = client.agents.sessions.create(
    model="claude-opus-4-8",
    system="You are a senior engineer. Complete the task autonomously.",
    dreaming=True,  # enable cross-session memory curation
    tools=[{"type": "bash"}, {"type": "file_editor"}],
)

print(f"Session ID: {session.id}")

# Start a task
run = client.agents.sessions.runs.create(
    session_id=session.id,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Migrate all API handlers to async/await."}],
)

print(f"Run ID: {run.id} — Status: {run.status}")
```

## Configure a webhook for lifecycle events

```python
# Register a webhook endpoint (do this once per project)
webhook = client.agents.webhooks.create(
    url="https://your-server.example.com/claude-webhooks",
    events=["run.completed", "run.failed", "run.requires_action"],
)
print(f"Webhook ID: {webhook.id}")
```

## Monitor execution in Claude Console

```
console.anthropic.com > Agents > Sessions > [your session ID]
```

The console shows the full subagent dispatch tree, tool calls, and memory writes in real time.

**Gotcha:** Dreaming runs on a schedule set by Anthropic (not real-time). Memory from the current session is not available to the same session mid-run — it becomes available to *future* sessions. Design your prompts so the current run is self-contained; use Dreaming to accumulate cross-run learning, not intra-run state.

**Gotcha 2:** Doubled rate limits apply to Claude Code CLI sessions, not raw API calls. If you are hitting rate limits on the API directly, submit a limit increase request via Console.
